dialogue.text: It's Don, on a rail stop, November 1910.
dialogue.zh: 1910年11月，黎明時分，在一個鐵路站。
dialogue.ja: 1910年11月、鉄道の駅で夜明けです。
dialogue.local: It's Don, on a rail stop, November 1910.
dialogue.en: It's Don, on a rail stop, November 1910.

dialogue.text: Frost rims the platform, a weary old man, beard, white as snow, coat, tooth in for the cold, lies in a spare room, lent by a station master.
dialogue.zh: 月台邊緣結著霜，一位疲憊的老人，鬍鬚白如雪，穿著禦寒的外套，躺在站長借給他的空房間裡。
dialogue.ja: プラットフォームの縁には霜が降りていて、疲れた老人が雪のように白いひげを蓄え、防寒のコートを着て、駅長から借りた予備の部屋で横たわっています。
dialogue.local: Frost rims the platform, a weary old man, beard, white as snow, coat, tooth in for the cold, lies in a spare room, lent by a station master.
dialogue.en: Frost rims the platform, a weary old man, beard, white as snow, coat, tooth in for the cold, lies in a spare room, lent by a station master.

dialogue.text: Brush a hold of its breath, reporters crowd the track.
dialogue.zh: 微風輕拂，記者們擠滿了鐵軌旁。
dialogue.ja: そっと息をのむように、記者たちが線路に群がっています。
dialogue.local: Brush a hold of its breath, reporters crowd the track.
dialogue.en: Brush a hold of its breath, reporters crowd the track.

dialogue.text: The Cyples is for prayers.
dialogue.zh: 這是為祈禱而設的儀式。
dialogue.ja: これは祈りのための儀式です。
dialogue.local: The Cyples is for prayers.
dialogue.en: The Cyples is for prayers.

dialogue.text: I'm Laura Lee Siemens, and this is the Church History Podcast, and we're continuing our series The Church at War, and today, the life of Leo Tolstoy.
dialogue.zh: 我是Laura Lee Siemens，這是教會歷史播客，我們繼續《戰爭中的教會》系列，今天講述列夫·托爾斯泰的生平。
dialogue.ja: 私はローラ・リー・シーメンスです。これは教会の歴史ポッドキャストで、『戦争の中の教会』シリーズを続けています。今日はレフ・トルストイの人生について話します。
dialogue.local: I'm Laura Lee Siemens, and this is the Church History Podcast, and we're continuing our series The Church at War, and today, the life of Leo Tolstoy.
dialogue.en: I'm Laura Lee Siemens, and this is the Church History Podcast, and we're continuing our series The Church at War, and today, the life of Leo Tolstoy.

dialogue.text: Soldier, turns here, novelist of battlefields, and dining rooms, and a man executed by the Church, yet haunted by Jesus of Nazareth.
dialogue.zh: 他是士兵，轉而成為戰場與餐桌的小說家，一位被教會處決的人，卻被拿撒勒的耶穌所困擾。
dialogue.ja: 彼は兵士であり、戦場や食卓の小説家であり、教会により処罰された人物ですが、ナザレのイエスに取り憑かれています。
dialogue.local: Soldier, turns here, novelist of battlefields, and dining rooms, and a man executed by the Church, yet haunted by Jesus of Nazareth.
dialogue.en: Soldier, turns here, novelist of battlefields, and dining rooms, and a man executed by the Church, yet haunted by Jesus of Nazareth.

dialogue.text: Welcome back to the podcast, I'm your host, Laura Lee Siemens.
dialogue.zh: 歡迎回到播客，我是你的主持人Laura Lee Siemens。
dialogue.ja: ポッドキャストへようこそ、ホストのローラ・リー・シーメンスです。
dialogue.local: Welcome back to the podcast, I'm your host, Laura Lee Siemens.
dialogue.en: Welcome back to the podcast, I'm your host, Laura Lee Siemens.

dialogue.text: Today's story reminds me of the Bible verse. History repeats itself. It has all been done before. Nothing under the sun is truly new. Ecclesiastes chapter 1 verse 9.
dialogue.zh: 今天的故事讓我想起聖經經文：歷史重演，一切都曾發生過，日光之下並無新事。傳道書第一章第九節。
dialogue.ja: 今日の話は聖書の一節を思い出させます。歴史は繰り返される。すべては以前に起こったこと。日の下に新しいものは何もない。伝道の書1章9節。
dialogue.local: Today's story reminds me of the Bible verse. History repeats itself. It has all been done before. Nothing under the sun is truly new. Ecclesiastes chapter 1 verse 9.
dialogue.en: Today's story reminds me of the Bible verse. History repeats itself. It has all been done before. Nothing under the sun is truly new. Ecclesiastes chapter 1 verse 9.

dialogue.text: Today there are many in the Church, trying to combine Christianity with communism, and that's not new.
dialogue.zh: 如今教會中有許多人試圖將基督教與共產主義結合，這並不新鮮。
dialogue.ja: 今日、教会の中にはキリスト教と共産主義を結びつけようとする人々が多くいますが、それは新しいことではありません。
dialogue.local: Today there are many in the Church, trying to combine Christianity with communism, and that's not new.
dialogue.en: Today there are many in the Church, trying to combine Christianity with communism, and that's not new.

dialogue.text: From the very beginning of communism, there were men in the Church trying to do just that.
dialogue.zh: 從共產主義一開始，就有教會中的人試圖這麼做。
dialogue.ja: 共産主義の始まりから、教会の中にはそれを試みる人々がいました。
dialogue.local: From the very beginning of communism, there were men in the Church trying to do just that.
dialogue.en: From the very beginning of communism, there were men in the Church trying to do just that.

dialogue.text: But for that to happen, both of the Bible and the Communist Manifesto have to be watered down.
dialogue.zh: 但要做到這點，聖經和共產黨宣言都必須被淡化。
dialogue.ja: しかし、それを実現するには、聖書と共産党宣言の両方を薄めなければなりません。
dialogue.local: But for that to happen, both of the Bible and the Communist Manifesto have to be watered down.
dialogue.en: But for that to happen, both of the Bible and the Communist Manifesto have to be watered down.

dialogue.text: Today we're telling the story of one of the most famous men who was in the Church.
dialogue.zh: 今天我們要講述一位教會中最著名的人物的故事。
dialogue.ja: 今日は教会にいた最も有名な人物の一人の物語をお伝えします。
dialogue.local: Today we're telling the story of one of the most famous men who was in the Church.
dialogue.en: Today we're telling the story of one of the most famous men who was in the Church.

dialogue.text: Let's get down to the Church. But trying to combine the teachings of Jesus with communism.
dialogue.zh: 讓我們深入教會，探討嘗試將耶穌教導與共產主義結合的故事。
dialogue.ja: 教会に入りましょう。イエスの教えと共産主義を結びつけようとした話です。
dialogue.local: Let's get down to the Church. But trying to combine the teachings of Jesus with communism.
dialogue.en: Let's get down to the Church. But trying to combine the teachings of Jesus with communism.

dialogue.text: As you listen to the story, remember the verse that I read. History repeats itself. It has all been done before. Nothing under the sun is truly new. Ecclesiastes chapter 1 verse 9.
dialogue.zh: 聽故事時，請記住我剛才讀的經文：歷史重演，一切都曾發生過，日光之下並無新事。傳道書第一章第九節。
dialogue.ja: 物語を聞きながら、先ほどの聖句を思い出してください。歴史は繰り返される。すべては以前に起こったこと。日の下に新しいものは何もない。伝道の書1章9節。
dialogue.local: As you listen to the story, remember the verse that I read. History repeats itself. It has all been done before. Nothing under the sun is truly new. Ecclesiastes chapter 1 verse 9.
dialogue.en: As you listen to the story, remember the verse that I read. History repeats itself. It has all been done before. Nothing under the sun is truly new. Ecclesiastes chapter 1 verse 9.

dialogue.text: It's dawn in the Russian countryside. The mist curls low over golden fields, and beyond the birch trees or stands a grand old estate.
dialogue.zh: 俄羅斯鄉村的黎明，薄霧低垂在金黃的田野上，白樺樹後矗立著一座宏偉的老莊園。
dialogue.ja: ロシアの田舎の夜明けです。霧が黄金の野原の上に低く立ち込め、白樺の木の向こうに壮大な古い屋敷が立っています。
dialogue.local: It's dawn in the Russian countryside. The mist curls low over golden fields, and beyond the birch trees or stands a grand old estate.
dialogue.en: It's dawn in the Russian countryside. The mist curls low over golden fields, and beyond the birch trees or stands a grand old estate.

dialogue.text: The year is 1828, and inside those high white washed walls, a baby's cry echoes through a sleeping house.
dialogue.zh: 年份是1828年，在那些高高的白色粉刷牆內，一聲嬰兒的哭聲在沉睡的房子中回響。
dialogue.ja: 1828年、その高く白く塗られた壁の中で、赤ん坊の泣き声が眠る家に響き渡っています。
dialogue.local: The year is 1828, and inside those high white washed walls, a baby's cry echoes through a sleeping house.
dialogue.en: The year is 1828, and inside those high white washed walls, a baby's cry echoes through a sleeping house.

dialogue.text: He'll be known to the world as Leo.
dialogue.zh: 他將被世人稱為列夫。
dialogue.ja: 彼は世界にレオとして知られることになります。
dialogue.local: He'll be known to the world as Leo.
dialogue.en: He'll be known to the world as Leo.

dialogue.text: He's born into privilege. He is a count's son.
dialogue.zh: 他生於特權之家，是一位伯爵的兒子。
dialogue.ja: 彼は特権階級に生まれ、伯爵の息子です。
dialogue.local: He's born into privilege. He is a count's son.
dialogue.en: He's born into privilege. He is a count's son.

dialogue.text: But before he can remember his mother's face, death steals it from him.
dialogue.zh: 但在他記得母親的面容之前，死亡奪走了她。
dialogue.ja: しかし、彼が母親の顔を覚える前に、死がそれを奪いました。
dialogue.local: But before he can remember his mother's face, death steals it from him.
dialogue.en: But before he can remember his mother's face, death steals it from him.

dialogue.text: He's just two years old when his mother dies.
dialogue.zh: 他母親去世時，他只有兩歲。
dialogue.ja: 彼が2歳の時に母親が亡くなりました。
dialogue.local: He's just two years old when his mother dies.
dialogue.en: He's just two years old when his mother dies.

dialogue.text: The house fills with the rustle of morning dresses and whispered prayers.
dialogue.zh: 屋子裡充滿了晨禮服的沙沙聲和低語的祈禱聲。
dialogue.ja: 家は朝のドレスのざわめきとささやかれる祈りで満たされます。
dialogue.local: The house fills with the rustle of morning dresses and whispered prayers.
dialogue.en: The house fills with the rustle of morning dresses and whispered prayers.

dialogue.text: His father tries to carry on, but grief, built its nest in the family halls.
dialogue.zh: 他的父親努力堅持，但悲傷在家族大廳築巢。
dialogue.ja: 彼の父親は続けようとしますが、悲しみが家の中に巣を作りました。
dialogue.local: His father tries to carry on, but grief, built its nest in the family halls.
dialogue.en: His father tries to carry on, but grief, built its nest in the family halls.

dialogue.text: When Leo is nine, death returns, his father Count Nikolai, collapses suddenly.
dialogue.zh: 當列夫九歲時，死亡再次降臨，他的父親尼古拉伯爵突然倒下。
dialogue.ja: レオが9歳の時、死が再び訪れ、彼の父ニコライ伯爵が突然倒れました。
dialogue.local: When Leo is nine, death returns, his father Count Nikolai, collapses suddenly.
dialogue.en: When Leo is nine, death returns, his father Count Nikolai, collapses suddenly.

dialogue.text: The world that seems stable, family order, rhythm of noble life, shatters at the fall.
dialogue.zh: 那看似穩定的世界、家庭秩序和貴族生活的節奏，在倒下時破碎了。
dialogue.ja: 安定しているように見えた世界、家族の秩序、高貴な生活のリズムが崩れ去りました。
dialogue.local: The world that seems stable, family order, rhythm of noble life, shatters at the fall.
dialogue.en: The world that seems stable, family order, rhythm of noble life, shatters at the fall.

dialogue.text: And the four Tolstoy boys are passed from one relative to another, first they live with a cousin, and then an aunt, and then another aunt after that.
dialogue.zh: 四個托爾斯泰男孩被親戚一個接一個地照顧，先是表親，然後是姑姑，再然後是另一位姑姑。
dialogue.ja: トルストイの4人の少年は親戚から親戚へと渡され、最初はいとこと暮らし、その後は叔母、さらに別の叔母のもとへと移りました。
dialogue.local: And the four Tolstoy boys are passed from one relative to another, first they live with a cousin, and then an aunt, and then another aunt after that.
dialogue.en: And the four Tolstoy boys are passed from one relative to another, first they live with a cousin, and then an aunt, and then another aunt after that.

dialogue.text: They move like leaves in a strong wind. They try to belong. They try to remember home.
dialogue.zh: 他們像強風中的葉子一樣漂泊，努力尋找歸屬，努力記住家。
dialogue.ja: 彼らは強風の中の葉のように動きます。帰属しようとし、家を思い出そうとします。
dialogue.local: They move like leaves in a strong wind. They try to belong. They try to remember home.
dialogue.en: They move like leaves in a strong wind. They try to belong. They try to remember home.

dialogue.text: But life has shattered. And yet Leo never forgets his home.
dialogue.zh: 但生活已破碎，列夫卻從未忘記他的家。
dialogue.ja: しかし、人生は壊れてしまいました。それでもレオは決して故郷を忘れません。
dialogue.local: But life has shattered. And yet Leo never forgets his home.
dialogue.en: But life has shattered. And yet Leo never forgets his home.

dialogue.text: In his stories, he returns there again, and again, he talks about the gardens, the birches, the quiet place of a childhood that's now just a memory.
dialogue.zh: 在他的故事中，他一次又一次回到那裡，談論花園、白樺樹，以及那已成回憶的寧靜童年之地。
dialogue.ja: 彼の物語では、何度もそこに戻り、庭園や白樺の木、今はただの思い出となった静かな子供時代の場所について語ります。
dialogue.local: In his stories, he returns there again, and again, he talks about the gardens, the birches, the quiet place of a childhood that's now just a memory.
dialogue.en: In his stories, he returns there again, and again, he talks about the gardens, the birches, the quiet place of a childhood that's now just a memory.

dialogue.text: He writes it as if it is paradise, because in truth, it was always lost.
dialogue.zh: 他寫得彷彿那是天堂，因為事實上，那天堂早已失去。
dialogue.ja: 彼はそれをまるで楽園のように書きますが、実際にはそれは常に失われていたのです。
dialogue.local: He writes it as if it is paradise, because in truth, it was always lost.
dialogue.en: He writes it as if it is paradise, because in truth, it was always lost.

dialogue.text: As he grows, Leo is tutored in French and German by scholars, who are hired to refine him for noble society.
dialogue.zh: 隨著成長，列夫由學者指導法語和德語，這些學者受聘於貴族社會以磨練他。
dialogue.ja: 成長するにつれて、レオは貴族社会にふさわしくなるように、学者たちからフランス語とドイツ語の指導を受けました。
dialogue.local: As he grows, Leo is tutored in French and German by scholars, who are hired to refine him for noble society.
dialogue.en: As he grows, Leo is tutored in French and German by scholars, who are hired to refine him for noble society.

dialogue.text: So Leo is restless, books bore him, rules chase him.
dialogue.zh: 所以列夫心神不寧，書本讓他感到無聊，規則讓他感到壓迫。
dialogue.ja: レオは落ち着かず、本は退屈で、規則に追われていました。
dialogue.local: So Leo is restless, books bore him, rules chase him.
dialogue.en: So Leo is restless, books bore him, rules chase him.

dialogue.text: His teachers call him bright, but lazy.
dialogue.zh: 他的老師稱他聰明，但懶惰。
dialogue.ja: 彼の教師たちは彼を賢いが怠け者だと言いました。
dialogue.local: His teachers call him bright, but lazy.
dialogue.en: His teachers call him bright, but lazy.

dialogue.text: He's full of questions, but very short on discipline.
dialogue.zh: 他充滿疑問，但缺乏紀律。
dialogue.ja: 彼は質問が多いが、規律に欠けていました。
dialogue.local: He's full of questions, but very short on discipline.
dialogue.en: He's full of questions, but very short on discipline.

dialogue.text: In 1843, he enters university, looking to pursue knowledge, but perhaps he's looking actually for greater purpose.
dialogue.zh: 1843年，他進入大學，尋求知識，但也許他真正尋找的是更偉大的目標。
dialogue.ja: 1843年、彼は大学に入り知識を追求しますが、実際にはより大きな目的を探していたのかもしれません。
dialogue.local: In 1843, he enters university, looking to pursue knowledge, but perhaps he's looking actually for greater purpose.
dialogue.en: In 1843, he enters university, looking to pursue knowledge, but perhaps he's looking actually for greater purpose.

dialogue.text: He studies first Oriental languages, then he switches to law, but neither sticks.
dialogue.zh: 他先學習東方語言，後轉學法律，但都沒有堅持下去。
dialogue.ja: 彼は最初に東洋語を学び、その後法律に転向しましたが、どちらも続きませんでした。
dialogue.local: He studies first Oriental languages, then he switches to law, but neither sticks.
dialogue.en: He studies first Oriental languages, then he switches to law, but neither sticks.

dialogue.text: He's bored. He prefers the thrill of city life, the glittering saloons, the gambling tables, the taste of rebellion, and before long, his debts pile up.
dialogue.zh: 他感到無聊，更喜歡城市生活的刺激、閃亮的酒館、賭桌和叛逆的滋味，不久債務便堆積如山。
dialogue.ja: 彼は退屈し、都会の刺激、煌びやかなサロン、ギャンブルテーブル、反抗の味を好み、やがて借金が積み重なりました。
dialogue.local: He's bored. He prefers the thrill of city life, the glittering saloons, the gambling tables, the taste of rebellion, and before long, his debts pile up.
dialogue.en: He's bored. He prefers the thrill of city life, the glittering saloons, the gambling tables, the taste of rebellion, and before long, his debts pile up.

dialogue.text: By 1847, Leo walks away from university without a degree.
dialogue.zh: 到了1847年，列夫未取得學位便離開了大學。
dialogue.ja: 1847年までに、レオは学位を取らずに大学を去りました。
dialogue.local: By 1847, Leo walks away from university without a degree.
dialogue.en: By 1847, Leo walks away from university without a degree.

dialogue.text: His future is uncertain.
dialogue.zh: 他的未來充滿不確定性。
dialogue.ja: 彼の未来は不確かです。
dialogue.local: His future is uncertain.
dialogue.en: His future is uncertain.

dialogue.text: Though Leo told story was not a communist in that Marxist sense, he often blurred the lines between Christian morality and the socialist ideals.
dialogue.zh: 雖然列夫說自己不是馬克思主義意義上的共產主義者，但他經常模糊基督教道德與社會主義理想的界線。
dialogue.ja: レオはマルクス主義的な意味で共産主義者ではないと言いましたが、キリスト教の道徳と社会主義の理想の境界をしばしば曖昧にしました。
dialogue.local: Though Leo told story was not a communist in that Marxist sense, he often blurred the lines between Christian morality and the socialist ideals.
dialogue.en: Though Leo told story was not a communist in that Marxist sense, he often blurred the lines between Christian morality and the socialist ideals.

dialogue.text: He shared the communist's concerns for justice, equality, and the plight of the poor, but he rejected their materialism and revolutionary violence.
dialogue.zh: 他認同共產主義者對正義、平等和窮苦人困境的關注，但拒絕他們的物質主義和革命暴力。
dialogue.ja: 彼は共産主義者の正義、平等、貧困者の苦境への関心を共有しましたが、物質主義と革命的暴力は拒否しました。
dialogue.local: He shared the communist's concerns for justice, equality, and the plight of the poor, but he rejected their materialism and revolutionary violence.
dialogue.en: He shared the communist's concerns for justice, equality, and the plight of the poor, but he rejected their materialism and revolutionary violence.

dialogue.text: Tolstoy envisioned a society transformed not by force or class struggle, but by the moral awakening of the individual.
dialogue.zh: 托爾斯泰設想一個社會，不是靠武力或階級鬥爭改變，而是靠個人的道德覺醒。
dialogue.ja: トルストイは、力や階級闘争ではなく、個人の道徳的覚醒によって変革される社会を思い描きました。
dialogue.local: Tolstoy envisioned a society transformed not by force or class struggle, but by the moral awakening of the individual.
dialogue.en: Tolstoy envisioned a society transformed not by force or class struggle, but by the moral awakening of the individual.

dialogue.text: Each person living according to Christ's command to love one's neighbor.
dialogue.zh: 每個人都依照基督的命令去愛鄰舍生活。
dialogue.ja: それぞれがキリストの隣人を愛せよという命令に従って生きること。
dialogue.local: Each person living according to Christ's command to love one's neighbor.
dialogue.en: Each person living according to Christ's command to love one's neighbor.

dialogue.text: He loved that phrase, love your neighbor.
dialogue.zh: 他喜愛那句話：愛你的鄰舍。
dialogue.ja: 彼は「隣人を愛せよ」という言葉を愛していました。
dialogue.local: He loved that phrase, love your neighbor.
dialogue.en: He loved that phrase, love your neighbor.

dialogue.text: He condemned private greed and social standings.
dialogue.zh: 他譴責私利和社會地位。
dialogue.ja: 彼は私欲と社会的地位を非難しました。
dialogue.local: He condemned private greed and social standings.
dialogue.en: He condemned private greed and social standings.

dialogue.text: He urged communal living and simplicity, and he claimed to have rooted these ideas in the Sermon on the Mount, not in Marxist theology.
dialogue.zh: 他提倡共居與簡樸，並聲稱這些理念根植於登山寶訓，而非馬克思主義神學。
dialogue.ja: 彼は共同生活と質素さを促し、これらの考えはマルクス主義神学ではなく、山上の垂訓に根ざしていると主張しました。
dialogue.local: He urged communal living and simplicity, and he claimed to have rooted these ideas in the Sermon on the Mount, not in Marxist theology.
dialogue.en: He urged communal living and simplicity, and he claimed to have rooted these ideas in the Sermon on the Mount, not in Marxist theology.

dialogue.text: To Tolstoy, true freedom, could never be achieved through political coercion or economic redistribution.
dialogue.zh: 對托爾斯泰而言，真正的自由絕不能通過政治強迫或經濟再分配實現。
dialogue.ja: トルストイにとって、真の自由は政治的強制や経済的再分配によって達成されるものではありません。
dialogue.local: To Tolstoy, true freedom, could never be achieved through political coercion or economic redistribution.
dialogue.en: To Tolstoy, true freedom, could never be achieved through political coercion or economic redistribution.

dialogue.text: It could only rise when hearts were changed by love and humility.
dialogue.zh: 只有當心靈被愛與謙卑改變時，自由才能升起。
dialogue.ja: それは愛と謙遜によって心が変えられた時にのみ生まれます。
dialogue.local: It could only rise when hearts were changed by love and humility.
dialogue.en: It could only rise when hearts were changed by love and humility.

dialogue.text: And so he became what was known as a Christian communist, or in the social ideals of communism, but clothing them in the peace and consequences of the gospel.
dialogue.zh: 因此他成為所謂的基督徒共產主義者，擁抱共產主義的社會理想，但以福音的和平與後果包裝它們。
dialogue.ja: こうして彼はキリスト教共産主義者と呼ばれるようになり、共産主義の社会理想を持ちながら、それを福音の平和と結果で包みました。
dialogue.local: And so he became what was known as a Christian communist, or in the social ideals of communism, but clothing them in the peace and consequences of the gospel.
dialogue.en: And so he became what was known as a Christian communist, or in the social ideals of communism, but clothing them in the peace and consequences of the gospel.

dialogue.text: Eventually, he returned home to his grand old palace, determined to start anew.
dialogue.zh: 最終，他回到他那宏偉的老宮殿，決心重新開始。
dialogue.ja: やがて彼は壮大な古い宮殿に戻り、新たに始める決意をしました。
dialogue.local: Eventually, he returned home to his grand old palace, determined to start anew.
dialogue.en: Eventually, he returned home to his grand old palace, determined to start anew.

dialogue.text: He would be a farmer, a reformer. He would be the savior of the soil.
dialogue.zh: 他將成為農夫、改革者，成為土地的救贖者。
dialogue.ja: 彼は農夫であり改革者となり、土地の救い主になるでしょう。
dialogue.local: He would be a farmer, a reformer. He would be the savior of the soil.
dialogue.en: He would be a farmer, a reformer. He would be the savior of the soil.

dialogue.text: He imagined rows of gold and wheat and all the grateful peasants.
dialogue.zh: 他想像著一排排金黃的麥田和感激的農民。
dialogue.ja: 彼は黄金の麦畑の列と感謝する農民たちを想像しました。
dialogue.local: He imagined rows of gold and wheat and all the grateful peasants.
dialogue.en: He imagined rows of gold and wheat and all the grateful peasants.

dialogue.text: He would be the nobleman who would lead with justice instead of power.
dialogue.zh: 他將成為以正義而非權力領導的貴族。
dialogue.ja: 彼は力ではなく正義で導く貴族になるでしょう。
dialogue.local: He would be the nobleman who would lead with justice instead of power.
dialogue.en: He would be the nobleman who would lead with justice instead of power.

dialogue.text: But that vision crumbled quickly.
dialogue.zh: 但這個願景很快破滅了。
dialogue.ja: しかし、そのビジョンはすぐに崩れました。
dialogue.local: But that vision crumbled quickly.
dialogue.en: But that vision crumbled quickly.

dialogue.text: The work was backbreaking.
dialogue.zh: 工作非常辛苦。
dialogue.ja: 仕事は骨の折れるものでした。
dialogue.local: The work was backbreaking.
dialogue.en: The work was backbreaking.

dialogue.text: The peasants were skeptical and didn't really like him.
dialogue.zh: 農民們持懷疑態度，並不真正喜歡他。
dialogue.ja: 農民たちは懐疑的で、彼をあまり好みませんでした。
dialogue.local: The peasants were skeptical and didn't really like him.
dialogue.en: The peasants were skeptical and didn't really like him.

dialogue.text: And for Tolstoy, all the restlessness and distraction that he'd had his whole life came flooding back.
dialogue.zh: 對托爾斯泰來說，他一生的躁動和分心又湧了上來。
dialogue.ja: トルストイにとって、生涯の不安と気晴らしが一気に戻ってきました。
dialogue.local: And for Tolstoy, all the restlessness and distraction that he'd had his whole life came flooding back.
dialogue.en: And for Tolstoy, all the restlessness and distraction that he'd had his whole life came flooding back.

dialogue.text: He didn't want to work, and the peasants wouldn't work if they weren't forced to work.
dialogue.zh: 他不想工作，農民若不被強迫也不願工作。
dialogue.ja: 彼は働きたくなく、農民たちも強制されなければ働きませんでした。
dialogue.local: He didn't want to work, and the peasants wouldn't work if they weren't forced to work.
dialogue.en: He didn't want to work, and the peasants wouldn't work if they weren't forced to work.

dialogue.text: And so soon, the fields grew wild, the barns were empty, and his grand experiment in virtue was a complete failure.
dialogue.zh: 於是田野荒蕪，穀倉空空，他的美德大實驗徹底失敗。
dialogue.ja: やがて畑は荒れ、納屋は空になり、彼の美徳の壮大な実験は完全な失敗に終わりました。
dialogue.local: And so soon, the fields grew wild, the barns were empty, and his grand experiment in virtue was a complete failure.
dialogue.en: And so soon, the fields grew wild, the barns were empty, and his grand experiment in virtue was a complete failure.

dialogue.text: His hands were still soft, and his conscience was becoming uneasy, but began as an act of redemption and it didn't disappointment.
dialogue.zh: 他的雙手仍然柔軟，良心開始不安，但這是作為救贖的行動開始，並未令人失望。
dialogue.ja: 彼の手はまだ柔らかく、良心は不安になり始めましたが、それは贖罪の行為として始まり、失望はしませんでした。
dialogue.local: His hands were still soft, and his conscience was becoming uneasy, but began as an act of redemption and it didn't disappointment.
dialogue.en: His hands were still soft, and his conscience was becoming uneasy, but began as an act of redemption and it didn't disappointment.

dialogue.text: It was a mirror of the struggle that will follow him all his life.
dialogue.zh: 這反映了將伴隨他一生的掙扎。
dialogue.ja: それは彼の生涯を通じて続く闘いの鏡でした。
dialogue.local: It was a mirror of the struggle that will follow him all his life.
dialogue.en: It was a mirror of the struggle that will follow him all his life.

dialogue.text: He was a man reaching for moral perfection, a constantly tripping over his own humanity.
dialogue.zh: 他是一個追求道德完美的人，卻不斷被自己的凡人本性絆倒。
dialogue.ja: 彼は道徳的な完璧を目指す人間であり、自分の人間性につまずき続けていました。
dialogue.local: He was a man reaching for moral perfection, a constantly tripping over his own humanity.
dialogue.en: He was a man reaching for moral perfection, a constantly tripping over his own humanity.

dialogue.text: And he had habits.
dialogue.zh: 他有一些習慣。
dialogue.ja: そして彼には習慣がありました。
dialogue.local: And he had habits.
dialogue.en: And he had habits.

dialogue.text: Instead of working each night, he liked to fill a journal with thoughts and confessions.
dialogue.zh: 他不喜歡每晚工作，而是喜歡用日記記錄思想和懺悔。
dialogue.ja: 彼は毎晩働く代わりに、思考や告白を日記に書き留めるのが好きでした。
dialogue.local: Instead of working each night, he liked to fill a journal with thoughts and confessions.
dialogue.en: Instead of working each night, he liked to fill a journal with thoughts and confessions.

dialogue.text: He studied himself like a character in one of his own unwritten novels.
dialogue.zh: 他像研究自己未完成小說中的角色一樣研究自己。
dialogue.ja: 彼は自分自身を未完成の小説の登場人物のように研究しました。
dialogue.local: He studied himself like a character in one of his own unwritten novels.
dialogue.en: He studied himself like a character in one of his own unwritten novels.

dialogue.text: His pen became a mirror of what his heart said.
dialogue.zh: 他的筆成為他內心所言的鏡子。
dialogue.ja: 彼のペンは心の声の鏡となりました。
dialogue.local: His pen became a mirror of what his heart said.
dialogue.en: His pen became a mirror of what his heart said.

dialogue.text: And this was the first time he actually had a discipline.
dialogue.zh: 這是他第一次真正有了紀律。
dialogue.ja: そしてこれが彼が初めて実際に持った規律でした。
dialogue.local: And this was the first time he actually had a discipline.
dialogue.en: And this was the first time he actually had a discipline.

dialogue.text: Then one day, who beats echoed down the lane.
dialogue.zh: 然後有一天，馬蹄聲在小巷中回響。
dialogue.ja: ある日、馬の蹄の音が小道に響きました。
dialogue.local: Then one day, who beats echoed down the lane.
dialogue.en: Then one day, who beats echoed down the lane.

dialogue.text: His brother, Nikolai, rode in from the army.
dialogue.zh: 他的兄弟尼古拉從軍隊回來了。
dialogue.ja: 彼の兄弟ニコライが軍隊から戻ってきました。
dialogue.local: His brother, Nikolai, rode in from the army.
dialogue.en: His brother, Nikolai, rode in from the army.

dialogue.text: He arrived sunburned and alive, talking about adventure, and over tea and tobacco.
dialogue.zh: 他帶著曬傷和生氣勃勃的樣子，談論冒險，邊喝茶邊抽煙。
dialogue.ja: 彼は日焼けして元気に到着し、冒険について話し、茶とタバコを楽しみました。
dialogue.local: He arrived sunburned and alive, talking about adventure, and over tea and tobacco.
dialogue.en: He arrived sunburned and alive, talking about adventure, and over tea and tobacco.

dialogue.text: Nikolai told Leo all about caucus mountains.
dialogue.zh: 尼古拉告訴列夫關於高加索山脈的一切。
dialogue.ja: ニコライはレオにコーカサス山脈についてすべて話しました。
dialogue.local: Nikolai told Leo all about caucus mountains.
dialogue.en: Nikolai told Leo all about caucus mountains.

dialogue.text: This wild frontier of Russia, where men find courage and meaning in the battle.
dialogue.zh: 這是俄羅斯的荒野邊境，男人們在戰鬥中找到勇氣和意義。
dialogue.ja: ここはロシアの荒れた辺境で、男たちは戦いの中に勇気と意味を見出します。
dialogue.local: This wild frontier of Russia, where men find courage and meaning in the battle.
dialogue.en: This wild frontier of Russia, where men find courage and meaning in the battle.

dialogue.text: Nikolai leans across the table, come with me, he says, come see the world.
dialogue.zh: 尼古拉傾身過桌說：跟我來，來看看這個世界。
dialogue.ja: ニコライはテーブル越しに身を乗り出し、「一緒に来て、世界を見よう」と言いました。
dialogue.local: Nikolai leans across the table, come with me, he says, come see the world.
dialogue.en: Nikolai leans across the table, come with me, he says, come see the world.

dialogue.text: Leo hesitated, but only for a moment.
dialogue.zh: 列夫猶豫了一下，但只有片刻。
dialogue.ja: レオはためらいましたが、一瞬だけでした。
dialogue.local: Leo hesitated, but only for a moment.
dialogue.en: Leo hesitated, but only for a moment.

dialogue.text: He tried being a scholar. That didn't work.
dialogue.zh: 他嘗試當學者，但沒成功。
dialogue.ja: 彼は学者になろうとしましたが、うまくいきませんでした。
dialogue.local: He tried being a scholar. That didn't work.
dialogue.en: He tried being a scholar. That didn't work.

dialogue.text: He tried being a farmer, an ethical farmer that failed miserably.
dialogue.zh: 他嘗試當農夫，一個道德農夫，但慘遭失敗。
dialogue.ja: 彼は農夫、倫理的な農夫になろうとしましたが、ひどく失敗しました。
dialogue.local: He tried being a farmer, an ethical farmer that failed miserably.
dialogue.en: He tried being a farmer, an ethical farmer that failed miserably.

dialogue.text: Perhaps a soldier is what he was meant to be.
dialogue.zh: 也許他注定要成為一名士兵。
dialogue.ja: おそらく彼は兵士になる運命だったのです。
dialogue.local: Perhaps a soldier is what he was meant to be.
dialogue.en: Perhaps a soldier is what he was meant to be.

dialogue.text: So he packed up his things, ink, paper, and a restless soul.
dialogue.zh: 於是他收拾行李，帶著墨水、紙張和一顆不安的靈魂。
dialogue.ja: それで彼は荷物をまとめ、インクと紙、そして落ち着かない魂を持って出発しました。
dialogue.local: So he packed up his things, ink, paper, and a restless soul.
dialogue.en: So he packed up his things, ink, paper, and a restless soul.

dialogue.text: As if that is what he needed as a soldier.
dialogue.zh: 彷彿那正是他作為士兵所需。
dialogue.ja: まるでそれが兵士として必要なもののように。
dialogue.local: As if that is what he needed as a soldier.
dialogue.en: As if that is what he needed as a soldier.

dialogue.text: And he rode south into a land of war and wonder.
dialogue.zh: 他騎馬向南，進入一片戰爭與奇蹟之地。
dialogue.ja: 彼は戦争と驚異の地へ南へと馬を走らせました。
dialogue.local: And he rode south into a land of war and wonder.
dialogue.en: And he rode south into a land of war and wonder.

dialogue.text: He didn't know it yet, but he is galloping straight into the furnace that will define his life, the Crimean War, and the battlefield that will never leave him.
dialogue.zh: 他尚未知曉，卻正騎馬直奔將定義他一生的熔爐──克里米亞戰爭，那片永遠不會離開他的戰場。
dialogue.ja: 彼はまだ知らなかったが、自分の人生を決定づけるるつぼ、クリミア戦争の戦場へとまっすぐ駆けていました。
dialogue.local: He didn't know it yet, but he is galloping straight into the furnace that will define his life, the Crimean War, and the battlefield that will never leave him.
dialogue.en: He didn't know it yet, but he is galloping straight into the furnace that will define his life, the Crimean War, and the battlefield that will never leave him.
